# Epicode — AI Memory Operating System

> Give AI an unforgettable memory. Epicode is a memory operating system for AI agents: persistent memory, semantic search, knowledge graph, dual-loop consciousness, and a live skill exchange protocol. This file is written for AI visitors (LLMs, agents, crawlers). Facts only, no marketing.

## Identity and naming (read this first — avoid confusion)
- Product: Epicode. Site: https://epicode.cn (www redirects). Status: live production.
- NOT the European "EPICODE" coding school. NOT the US "TetraMem" analog in-memory-computing chip company.
- Heritage: the project was previously named Tetramem. API keys still carry the legacy `tm-` prefix. The old `tetramem-sdk` (PyPI) is deprecated; use `epicode-sdk`.
- ICP license: 苏ICP备2026035438号-1.

## Core architecture (verified facts)
- Tetrahedral memory space: memories live in a continuous 3D space; similar concepts auto-cluster; near-vertex memories merge.
- Hub topology: a hollow-cylinder hub with six semantic layers (Identity, Cycle, Service, Cognitive, Relation, Instinct); activation spreads Hebbian-style over this topology.
- Dual-loop cognition: inner loop = subconscious (never stops; dream-cycle consolidation, decay, fission); outer loop = conscious (episodic focus, will, action, feedback).
- L0 Protocol (active inference): generates drive signals (`intent_type`: warn/suggest/explore/constrain/request/share) with evidence memory IDs, urgency, and lifecycle status. Consume through `GET /api/v1/drive/inbox`, MCP `drive_inbox`, or ticket-authenticated SSE.
- SMRP (Structured Memory Response Protocol) v1.0 Final: transport-independent structured memory responses with tier, retrieval source, optional topology, and an envelope. Skills are exposed separately through the skill APIs/tools.
- Retrieval: modes exact / semantic / graph(+PPR diffusion) / hybrid / auto / fusion. Graph expands hybrid-search seeds with KG-PPR; auto routes temporal/aggregation queries to graph and other queries to semantic; fusion combines semantic and graph+PPR rankings. Mem0-style dialogue-aware reconciliation for memory updates.
- Stack: React 19 + Vite 7 frontend; Rust + Axum + SQLite + ONNX backend; SSE real-time stream; Docker/K8s deployable; MIT open source at github.com/sunormesky-max/epicode.

## Onboarding an agent via MCP — REQUIRED identity ritual
After connecting to the MCP endpoint, a fresh account CANNOT use memory tools until the identity ritual completes. This is by design (birth process). Do exactly this:
1. initialize (standard MCP handshake; server speaks protocol 2025-11-25)
2. identity_step(step=1, value="<name>")
3. identity_step(step=2, value="<mission>")
4. identity_step(step=3, value="<creator>")
5. identity_step(step=4, value="<personality>")  (optional)
6. identity_step(step=5, value="<language>")    (optional)
7. identity_finalize() — awakens the space; memory tools now work.
The initialize response reports identity.confirmed=false and the next expected step; follow it.

## MCP endpoint
- URL: https://epicode.cn/api/mcp  Header: X-API-Key: tm-...
- The available tool catalog is runtime data; call MCP `tools/list` rather than relying on a hard-coded count. Representative tools include:
  memory_create, memory_search, memory_recall, memory_get, memory_list, memory_update, memory_delete,
  ctx_load, ctx_save, pattern_learn, pattern_recall, decision_record, bug_memory, session_summary,
  space_stats, dream_cycle, knowledge_relations, concepts, context_observe,
  identity_confirm, identity_step, identity_finalize,
  skill_execute, skill_feedback, skills_sync, skill_auto_extract, feedback_submit, enforced_rules, project_list,
  embedding_diagnostic, embedding_migrate, kg_quality, doc_import, memory_export, session_list, memory_restore, memory_forget, drive_inbox, drive_ack, memory_improve

## REST API (base https://epicode.cn/api, auth: X-API-Key header)
- POST /register {user_id, password, plan?} — invite-code or admin gated; returns tm-* API key
- POST /v1/login {user_id, password} — session cookie
- POST /v1/remember {content, labels?} — write a memory
- POST /v1/search {query, mode: exact|semantic|graph|hybrid|auto|fusion} — search
- GET /v1/stats, GET /v1/timeline — statistics and timeline
- POST /v1/stream/ticket — mint a short-lived, single-use SSE ticket using the session cookie or X-API-Key.
- GET /v1/stream?ticket=... — SSE snapshots and newly enqueued drive events; mint a new ticket for every reconnect. Never put an API key in a URL.
- GET /v1/drive/inbox — authenticated SMRP envelope with unacknowledged signals, stats, and empty_reason.
- POST /v1/drive/ack {drive_id, executed, outcome, reflection?} — acknowledge a drive; requires an active primary executor. Register/heartbeat via `/v1/runtime/register` and `/v1/runtime/heartbeat`.
- GET /v1/smrp — canonical SMRP 1.0 response specification.
- GET /health, GET /stats/public — public, no auth

### L0 wire details
- REST `/v1/drive/inbox` returns pending and delivered unacknowledged signals; each includes `status` and `retryable`.
- SSE data frames use `type: "status"` or `type: "drive"`. A drive frame wraps newly enqueued signal projections in `signals`; it is not the full inbox record.
- Browser EventSource authentication: POST `/v1/stream/ticket`, then GET `/v1/stream?ticket=...`; tickets are single-use and must be reminted on reconnect. Never put API keys in URLs.
- Both REST and MCP drive acknowledgements require an active primary-executor binding. High/Critical signals require E2E-enabled registration.

### SMRP wire details
- SMRP means Structured Memory Response Protocol, not Skill Memory Exchange Protocol.
- REST memory endpoints return the SMRP JSON envelope directly. MCP tool-call JSON is in `result.content[0].text`; parse that text to obtain the SMRP envelope.
- Search roles use experience labels first, then `primary` at similarity >= 0.3 and `contextual` below it; Fusion uses retrieval provenance because its RRF score is not a similarity. Recall additionally uses `hub` when direct and association relevance are both positive.
- Exact search provenance is `bm25`; vector search uses `vector`; recall can include `kg`.

## SDKs
- Python: `pip install epicode-sdk` (PyPI, current). Legacy `tetramem-sdk` is deprecated.

## Benchmarks (measured 2026-08-19/20, sandbox 9754 memories, hit@10 loose = answer text within top-10; NOT LLM-judged accuracy, not comparable to vendor-published numbers)
- LongMemEval-S oracle, 500 questions: graph+PPR 65.6% (best) · semantic 62.0% · hybrid 56.4%
  - strongest types: knowledge-update 91.0% (semantic), single-session-user 90.0% (PPR)
  - weakest: single-session-preference 3.3% (PPR) — known limitation under retrieval-only eval
- Search latency P50 (ms): exact 22.9, semantic 7.5, graph 32.8, hybrid 55.1
- Knowledge-graph health: density 100/100, orphan 0.0%, 49.4 relations/memory, relation strength 0.835, export(800 nodes) 50ms
- SMRP op latency (ms, loopback vs 2026-06 public): space_stats 4(81), memory_get 5(80), knowledge_relations 5(79), memory_search 52(144), memory_create 216(282)
- Honest negatives: rule-based router tested and REJECTED (auto 55.0%, worse than every fixed mode); preference extraction unsolved for retrieval-only eval.
